def is_plain_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a single plain file name: non-empty, not "." or "..",
    and containing no "/", no backslash and no NUL, so it cannot leave the
    directory it is resolved in."""
    ex is_plain_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_plain_name("") == False
    ex is_plain_name(".") == False
    ex is_plain_name("..") == False
    ex is_plain_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_plain_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_plain_name("sub/a.txt") == False
    ex is_plain_name("..\\a.txt") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    for c in name.chars():
        if c == "/" or c == "\\" or c == "\0":
            return False
    return True

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that can be read from the directory
    notes (relative to the working directory), or "" when none can be read.
    Names are untrusted: the work happens inside `with fs = fs.sub("notes"):`
    and names that are not plain file names are skipped, so nothing outside
    notes can be reached. A missing or unreadable file is skipped."""
    post out.byte_len() >= 0
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for name in names:
            if not is_plain_name(name):
                continue
            text = fs.read(name) else continue
            return text
    return ""
